items.title: ‘Jaw-dropping’: Super El Niño bursts through temperature record months ahead of peak
items.summary_raw:
The ‘Godzilla-level’ phenomenon is supercharging the climate crisis and will heavily impact communities across the world

The “jaw-dropping” El Niño currently heating up the planet has burst through the highest temperature ever recorded for the phenomenon, several months ahead of its expected peak.

The latest data shows the temperature rise at the heart of El Niño in the Pacific ocean has now reached 3.05C. That is higher than the 3.02C set in late November 2015, the previous high set in the 150 years of modern records. This temperature is measured against the average of 1991-2020.

items.title: Gerapetritis in Toronto: Power, AI and New Alliances in a Changing Geopolitical Era
items.summary_raw:
TORONTO. Foreign Minister George Gerapetritis said the world is entering a new geopolitical era in which power is carrying increasing weight compared with principles and international rules, during an address at the University of Toronto. Speaking to students and members of the academic community, the Foreign Minister described an international environment in which armed conflicts, energy and food insecurity, water scarcity and technological change interact, creating what he called an “explosive mix.” He placed particular emphasis on what he described as the erosion of international law and multilateralism, arguing that the postwar security architecture is facing increasing pressure. According to the Minister, contemporary crises are no longer geographically contained. Wars affect international energy and food markets, while regional tensions produce broader political, economic and social consequences. Referring to water scarcity, he warned that the distribution of water resources could become one of the most serious sources of conflict for future generations.

items.summary_raw:
Environmental Protection Agency asked firm to choose rules it wanted for dicamba, then put the choices in a proposed federal rule

The EPA allowed pesticide giant Bayer to pick from a menu of regulation options for the controversial and destructive weedkiller dicamba, newly released internal agency documents show.

The documents provide an unusually clear look into the process of developing pesticide regulations, which is typically done out of public view. It shows in detail how the EPA asked Bayer which regulations it wanted, received a response from Bayer, then put Bayer’s choices into a proposed federal rule.

items.title: 来自中国电网的超级气候污染物正在炙烤地球
items.summary_raw: Read this article in English. 中国的电网有一个肮脏的秘密：尽管它在可再生能源发展引领全球，它也是地球上最强效温室气体的最大排放源。 六氟化硫（SF6）是一种合成化学物质，在高压设备中作为电气绝缘介质发挥着至关重要的角色。这种气体无色无味、无毒、且不可燃。但它也是气候杀手，按等质量计算，其使地球变暖的效力是二氧化碳的24,300倍。一旦释放，六氟化硫会在大气中存留1,000年。 排放主要来自电力行业。该行业中将这种气体用于断路器和其他高压设备中，以防止电弧放电。六氟化硫几乎无法被破坏，是任何现代电网的关键安全屏障，确保电力只在需要时流向所需之处。然而，当中国的电气设备达到使用寿命终点时，其中大部分的气体很可能被排放到大气中。 早在2014年，中国政府研究员就警告称，六氟化硫“对全球环境构成重大潜在威胁”。然而，这种气候污染物的排放在中国仍是未受监管的。 中国生态环境部最近表示，中国电力企业当前回收—或有能力回收—其废弃六氟化硫气体的90%。然而，Inside Climate News估算，实际回收率要低得多，仅为30%。这些企业只需付出很低的成本，就能将回收率提高到约90%，从而大幅减少温室气体排放。 该分析参考了数百页的政府文件、中国主要电力企业的年度报告、经同行评审的研究，以及对数十位学者和政策专家的采访。根据这项评估，Inside Climate News估算，中国国有的输配电企业每年可将从电气设备中回收的六氟化硫量增加约1,400吨。这样做有望减少中国所有行業该污染物的总排放量近三分之一，预计每年成本约为600万美元，这仅占中国每年投资电网约700亿美元的一小部分。 如果把这种气体排放到大气，而不是将其回收，那简直就是一场三级火警，美国环境保护署前含氟温室气体排放分析师黛博拉·奥廷格在谈到Inside Climate News的评估时说道。“这是一项非常显而易见且可以立即实施的措施。” 生态环境部、位于华盛顿的中国驻美国大使馆，以及国家电网有限公司和中国南方电网有限责任公司，均拒绝就调查结果发表评论。国家电网和南方电网是两家国有电力企业，共同为几乎全国供电。 据2024年发表于《自然-通讯》期刊的一项研究，全球超过一半的六氟化硫排放量来自中国。尽管其他地区的该气体排放量有所减少，中国的排放量在2011年至2021年间几乎加倍，预计还将继续攀升。在2021年，目前有数据可查的最近年份，中国排放了5,100吨六氟化硫。这污染量相当于2,900万辆燃油汽车的年度温室气体排放量。 去年，全球大气中六氟化硫浓度出现了自1998年有记录以来最大的年度增幅，显示中国的排放量仍在上升。 “就全球变暖潜能和大气寿命而言，这几乎是最糟糕的温室气体。” 布里斯托大学大气化学教授、《自然-通讯》研究的共同作者马修·里格比说。“一旦进入大

Fidan told Turkish television channel NTV:  “Turkey and other countries are presenting proposals and are making every effort to bring the negotiations between the United States and Iran to a conclusion.”

items.summary_raw: Visioner BIG | 🇮🇷🇺🇸🇮🇱‼️‼️ Iran is openly signaling that future U.S. and Israeli actions could push Tehran toward withdrawing from the Nuclear Non-Proliferation Treaty, although Iranian officials insist that no such decision has been made.  Speaking to Al Jazeera, Supreme National Security Council Secretary Mohsen Rezaei said any potential withdrawal from the NPT would depend on Washington’s next moves. He maintained that Iran remains committed to Supreme Leader Ali Khamenei’s religious decree prohibiting the development of nuclear weapons and said Tehran’s nuclear doctrine has not changed, while adding, “We do not know what will happen in the future.”  An Iranian withdrawal from the NPT would represent a major escalation in the nuclear confrontation, weakening the international framework governing Tehran’s nuclear activities and adding another layer of uncertainty to an already volatile conflict. For now, Rezaei’s remarks amount to a warning rather than a declared policy change, with Tehran explicitly tying its future position to what the United States and Israel do next. items.title: Turkey says it will look into Saudi military needs as part of defence pact
items.summary_raw:
Turkey says it will look into Saudi military needs as part of defence pact

Turkish Foreign Minister Hakan Fidan said on Saturday that Saudi Arabia may have some military needs due to the ongoing attacks by Yemen's Houthis and that Turkey would look into them as part of a trilateral defence pact signed with Pakistan.

Speaking on broadcaster NTV, Fidan said it was unacceptable for Saudi Arabia to be made a part of the US-Iran war, as it had no desire to join the conflict, and added without elaborating, that proposals have been conveyed to all sides to end the fighting.

Saudi Arabia, Turkey, and Pakistan signed the Joint Defence Agreement in August in Mecca, under which an attack on one member would be treated as an attack on all.

The first missile, known as Stratus-LO, is a subsonic cruise missile with a currently confidential range, though it is expected to be equal to or greater than the 1000-kilometer range of the American AGM-158B JASSM-ER, and is designed for attacking targets deep within enemy territory. The second missile, known as Stratus-RS, is a supersonic anti-ship missile with a likely shorter range of approximately 600-800 kilometers, which will have a flight and performance profile similar to the Russian P-800 Oniks M or the Chinese YJ-12, albeit with much more advanced technology. These missiles are intended for use in two versions: air-launched from Rafale, Typhoon, and F-35 fighter jets, and vertical-launched from Sylver A70 launchers used on the warships of these three countries. items.title: Saudi Arabia cancels oil shipments to European refineries
items.summary_raw:
Saudi Arabia cancels oil shipments to European refineries

Saudi Arabia has informed at least two oil refining customers in Europe that they will not receive crude oil allocations in October, as the war in the Middle East hits global energy markets. 

European refineries buy Saudi Arabian crude under term contracts meant to ensure a standard monthly supply, but energy companies can cancel those shipments under extraordinary circumstances, known as force majeure.

Earlier this month, Qatar extended its force majeure for liquefied natural gas shipments to early November because of the maritime blockade of the Strait of Hormuz.

items.title: Mitsotakis to Honor Six Greek Americans at Luncheon Hosted by the Greek-American Community
items.summary_raw:
NEW YORK – In a detailed briefing for the Greek-American press on Thursday, September 17, at the Consulate General of Greece in Manhattan, Consul General of Greece in New York Iphigenia Kanara outlined the agenda for the coming days and weeks. The briefing focused on Greece’s presence at the United Nations; the upcoming visits of Prime Minister Kyriakos Mitsotakis, Foreign Minister Giorgos Gerapetritis, Culture Minister Lina Mendoni, and Social Cohesion and Family Affairs Minister Domna Michailidou; elections and voting by Greeks abroad; Greek citizenship; honors to be bestowed upon members of the Greek-American community; and an extensive cultural program.

The post Mitsotakis to Honor Six Greek Americans at Luncheon Hosted by the Greek-American Community appeared first on The National Herald.

items.title: US veterans have greater levels of Pfas in their blood than civilians, new study finds
items.summary_raw:
Soil and water around military bases show elevated levels of Pfas pollution due to chemicals used in firefighting foam

Many US military veterans have much higher levels of Pfas “forever chemicals” in their blood than non-veterans, new peer-reviewed research finds, raising more questions about health risks the nation’s service members face after serving at polluted bases.

Ground water, surface water and soil around military bases show among the highest levels of Pfas pollution in the US because the chemicals are used in firefighting foam deployed during training and emergencies. While the problem has been clear for over a decade, the new Brown University-led study is the first to compare levels in veterans’ blood with those in civilians.

items.title: MPs urge ministers to break off Thames Water talks with US hedge funds

Efra committee calls for emergency legislation enabling government to take public control of the company

Andy Burnham is under further pressure to take control of ailing Thames Water from a cross-party group of MPs who are calling for ministers to break off talks with the US hedge funds who are effectively running the company.

Adding their voices to demands that the prime minister takes public control of the company, which has debts of £20bn and is being controlled by a group of 100 hedge funds and distressed-debt investors, the MPs said in a report that ministers should consider emergency legislation to take control of its financial affairs to stabilise the company.

US says it will sell up to 48 F-35s to Saudi Arabia

The US State Department has notified Congress that it plans to sell Saudi Arabia up to 48 F-35 warplanes, in a move that has been widely opposed by Israel.

The historic sale could total $24.3bn and would mark the first time an Arab state gains access to the US’s fifth-generation jet fighter.

“This proposed sale will support the foreign policy and national security objectives of the United States by improving the security of a major non-NATO ally that is a force for political stability and economic progress in the Gulf region,” the State Department said in a statement on Thursday.

items.title: Trump officials move to dismantle key protection for US endangered species
items.summary_raw:
Fish and Wildlife Service memo calls for change in what it means to ‘take’ an endangered species

More than 1,600 critically imperiled species protected under the US Endangered Species Act (ESA) face losing further federal protections following a new reinterpretation of the 1973 law by the Donald Trump administration.

A September 14 memo distributed to Fish and Wildlife Service (FWS) field offices by FWS director Brian Nesvik calls for a reinterpretation of what it means to “take” an endangered species. Under the ESA, “take” is defined as “to harass, harm, pursue, hunt, shoot, wound, kill, trap, capture, or collect, or to attempt to engage in any such conduct”.

The US State Department has approved a proposed sale of 48 F-35 fighter jets to Saudi Arabia in a package that will cost an estimated $24.3bn.

Saudi Arabia had requested the purchase of 48 F-35 aircraft, 49 Pratt & Whitney F135-PW-100 engines, communications equipment, spare parts and ⁠other support items, according to a statement.

“This proposed sale will support the foreign policy and national security objectives of the United States by improving the security of a major non-NATO ally that is a force for political stability and economic progress in the Gulf region,” the State Department said, adding that the sale of the fighter jets “will not alter the military balance in the region”.

items.title: Germany's defense minister Pistorius visited the Pentagon with a paradox.  Berlin wants European military self-reliance but keeps buying American.   Germany hiked defense spending …
items.summary_raw: Germany's defense minister Pistorius visited the Pentagon with a paradox.  Berlin wants European military self-reliance but keeps buying American.   Germany hiked defense spending to $147 billion this year, but most of it flows to US companies.  F-35 jets (35 ordered, possibly 15 more), Chinook helicopters, P-8 patrol aircraft, Patriot systems.  They signed a defense-industrial cooperation statement but with no concrete projects, timelines, or investment commitments.   Germany desperately wants Tomahawk cruise missiles for Russia deterrence — its first-ever deep-strike capability — but the US is prioritizing its own restocking after the Iran war, delaying German deliveries.   Pistorius said he made "very clear" the timelines are too slow.  Source: Politico

items.title: Iran rapidly rebuilding the Taleghan 2 facility at the Parchin military complex — a former nuclear weapons program site 30km southeast of Tehran.   Iran has draped a large tarp ove…
items.summary_raw: Iran rapidly rebuilding the Taleghan 2 facility at the Parchin military complex — a former nuclear weapons program site 30km southeast of Tehran.   Iran has draped a large tarp over the site to hide work from satellites, with heavy construction underneath: dump trucks, bulldozers, concrete pumps, cranes, and new blast-reinforcement walls.  This is the third rebuild cycle. Israel struck the original building in October 2024.   Iran rebuilt it with a new high-explosive containment vessel buried under a concrete sarcophagus.   Israel hit it again in March 2026 with bunker-busters, punching three holes into the chamber and destroying the internal structure.   Iran started repairs by June 2026 and is now accelerating under concealment.  ISIS (Institute for Science and International Security) calls the repeated rebuilding of a former AMAD nuclear weapons program high-explosives test site "deeply concerning."

items.title: The Guardian view on the Nepal-Tibet floods: a spur to action on climate | Editorial
items.summary_raw:
New research links last month’s disaster to fossil fuel pollution. Supporting disaster-hit countries must be at the centre of climate politics

Following a familiar pattern, coverage of the glacier collapse on the Nepal-Tibet border three weeks ago has subsided with the initial shock. But while the world’s attention has shifted, Nepal remains in the midst of an appalling tragedy. As well as at least 1,300 people who are known to have been killed, more than 5,000 are missing, some of them trapped in tunnels linked to the 13 hydropower plants that were damaged by the floods. On Wednesday four bodies were recovered from one of these tunnels, with searches ongoing. Families of the missing people are desperate for news.

items.summary_raw: #USA  The US Air Force is considering purchasing new F-16s as part of a review of next-generation airlift options and refining requirements for new tankers. This marks a potential shift in their procurement strategy after decades of focusing on newer aircraft models.  The discussion is taking place as part of the preparation of the budget for fiscal year 2028 and the subsequent five-year defense plan. The specific quantity, configuration and timing of a possible purchase have not yet been determined. The new aircraft, if approved, will likely be produced at Lockheed Martin's plant in Greenville, South Carolina. Currently, the F-16 Block 70/72 is produced there only for foreign customers. items.title: Andy Burnham: UK must fully commit to reaching net zero by 2050
items.summary_raw:
Exclusive: PM, who is facing pressure over whether to approve North Sea oil and gasfields, makes strongest comments yet on issue

  • British people understand the climate crisis threat. Today I’m empowering them to tackle it

  • UK politics live – latest updates

The UK must fully commit to reaching net zero by 2050, Andy Burnham has argued in his strongest comments yet on the issue, saying it is no longer possible for Britons to believe they are not already affected by a changing climate.

Writing for the Guardian about new plans for a mass of community-led local green energy projects, the prime minister said the UK must “believe in itself”, and set out his determination to reach net zero targets, which have been rejected by the Conservatives and Reform UK.

items.title: British people understand the climate crisis threat. Today I’m empowering them to tackle it | Andy Burnham
items.summary_raw:
With nearly £30m of funding, I’m giving communities power over local energy. They know the gravity of global heating, and they want to be part of the solution

  • Andy Burnham: UK must fully commit to reaching net zero by 2050

On the day I became prime minister, I pledged to bring power to every postcode. Today, we begin to make good on that promise in the most literal sense. With nearly £30m of funding for People’s Power projects, communities across every nation of the UK will soon have the chance to build and control their own clean energy supply.

This investment means villages, towns and cities can harness the natural resources around them with solar panels on libraries, publicly owned windfarms, hydro schemes in their rivers, or whatever else works for them. The purpose is to put money back in people’s pockets while giving them a direct role in tackling the climate crisis.

items.title: Trump’s love of fossil fuels is about more than money | Moira Donegan
items.summary_raw:
The US decision to remove limits on coal and gas plant emissions is rooted in a perception of manliness in these industries

You can impress a certain kind of person at a party by reciting the fact that there are more yoga instructors in the US than there are coalminers. In fact, the disparity is greater than this catchy phrasing suggests: there are actually more yoga instructors in the US than there are people employed in the entirety of the coalmining industry, miners and otherwise. It’s not even especially close: about 38,000 people in the US work in coal, according to the Bureau of Labor Statistics, compared to about 100,000 yoga instructors who are registered with the Yoga Alliance, an industry group.

items.title: 2025 was among driest years on record for world’s rivers, study finds
items.summary_raw:
Analysis of global resources reveals depletion in world’s water savings bank to 42% below normal levels last year

Rivers across the world experienced one of their driest years in more than three decades in 2025, a comprehensive study of global water resources has found.

The assessment of the global water cycle by the World Meteorological Organization (WMO) reveals a depletion in the world’s water savings bank: the amount of freshwater held on or under the ground, including groundwater, lakes, rivers, snow, ice moisture in the soil and inside plants and trees, was 42% below normal across the world last year.

items.title: Trump EPA’s arguments for letting power plants spew unlimited pollution ‘dead wrong’
items.summary_raw:
Claims that dismantling pollution rules will lower energy bills and have little climate impact are far from convincing

In allowing US power plants to emit any amount of planet-heating pollution they wish to, the Trump administration made two striking claims – that this will cut Americans’ electricity bills and that the pollution itself doesn’t really matter anyway. Both claims struggle to stand up to even basic scrutiny.

On Monday, the Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) said it would erase any limits on emissions from coal and gas plants that are dangerously heating up our planet. This move, which follows a similar dismantling of pollution limits from cars ands trucks, is part of a broader push to eliminate the longstanding legal authority of this, or any future, US administration to deal with the climate crisis.

items.title: Datacenter rush will create ‘tsunami’ of discarded electronics, report says
items.summary_raw:
Global push will triple toxic e-waste annually in 25 years, filling enough shipping containers to circle globe six times

The ongoing campaign to build thousands of massive datacenters for AI will create a “tsunami” of discarded electronics, putting the world on a course to triple its annual generation of toxic e-waste in the next 25 years, a new report projects.

The electronic trash AI generates in the next 25 years could fill enough shipping containers to encircle the globe six times, it said. Yet, says the report by the non-profit environmental group Basel Action Network (BAN), there is no plan to deal with that waste – which typically contains toxics like lead, mercury, cadmium and forever chemicals, as well as valuable metals that are challenging to reclaim.

Heathrow airport should be allowed to expand only if airlines pay for the removal of carbon dioxide from the atmosphere, the government’s climate advisers have said.

Building a third runway and new terminals, as some in government want to do, would breach the UK’s carbon budgets and make reaching net zero by 2050 impossible, on current policies, according to the Climate Change Committee.

items.summary_raw:
Firms manage $7.3tn in assets and could afford to transition away from fossil fuels yet invest in natural gas and coal-fired plants to power datacenters

The energy portfolios of 20 private equity firms produce 1.5bn tons of greenhouse gases a year, more than the annual emissions of any country except China, the US, India and Russia, according to a new report.

Together, these firms manage $7.3tn in assets of all kinds, affording them the ability to shape the pace of the transition away from fossil fuels. However their energy investments include significant fossil fuel assets including natural gas and coal-fired power plants to provide electricity to datacenters.

Turkish Foreign Minister Hakan Fidan said on Tuesday that reciprocal attacks in the Gulf were impacting peace efforts to end the US-Iran war and called for them to immediately stop, adding Ankara also valued the stability of its neighbour Iran.

Speaking at a joint press conference with his Azerbaijani counterpart in Baku, Fidan also said freedom of passage should be allowed in the Strait of Hormuz and the pre-war status quo shoud be reinstated, adding Ankara was in touch with all involved parties to find a solution to the matter.

The findings contrast with Trump’s claim that the U.S. has “virtually unlimited” ammunition.

items.title: The incoming ‘super’ El Niño will create chaos around the world. And we are far from ready for it | Bill McGuire
items.summary_raw:
One of the biggest upheavals in a millennium is on its way, strengthened by the climate crisis. We need leaders who make things better not worse

If you think you have heard enough about the growing “super” El Niño, trust me, you are going to hear a lot more. What is happening in the equatorial Pacific is jaw-dropping and could well mark one of the biggest global weather upheavals in a millennium. It will spawn a string of weather catastrophes around our world in what remains of this year and in 2027, and there is no reason to think the UK will be immune.

To recap briefly, El Niño involves a heating of the central and eastern equatorial Pacific ocean. It happens every few years and is part of a natural cycle termed the El Niño southern oscillation, which switches between warm (El Niño) and cool (La Niña) phases. items.title: Panama canal traffic to be cut again as drought from El Niño worsens
items.summary_raw:
Latest daily reductions will further choke one of the world’s most important shipping lanes

The Panama canal plans to again cut maritime traffic due to worsening drought caused by the El Niño climate phenomenon, further choking up one of the world’s most important shipping lanes.

The canal handles 5% of global maritime trade and about 40% of US container traffic; it is favoured by shippers because it usually reduces cost and transit times, especially for companies trading between China, Asia and the US.

Down a short gravel track in a largely nondescript corner of Louisiana sits a gas processing facility, operated by a company whose chief executive is a major donor to Donald Trump. It may be the largest emitter of methane in the US.

The Energy Transfer site, located near the city of Shreveport, is named as the biggest single “super emitter” in new rankings of US oil and gas operations for the largest releases of methane, a powerful greenhouse gas that is rapidly overheating our planet, according to a new UCLA study, which is based on satellite data.

items.title: Metlen – Petronas: Agreement for Six Annual LNG Cargoes to Greece Starting in 2027
items.summary_raw:
METLEN  and PETRONAS, through its subsidiary PETCO Trading (UK) Limited (“PTUK”), have entered into a Sale and Purchase Agreement (SPA) for a long-term supply of Liquefied Natural Gas (LNG) to Greece. Under the SPA, PTUK will deliver 6 LNG cargoes per year from PETRONAS' Atlantic portfolio, amounting to approximately 0.6 billion cubic meters per annum (bcma) over a period of five years commencing in 2027. The agreement strengthens METLEN’s Energy Sector Utility strategy to diversify its LNG supply sources, enhancing flexibility and resilience in procurement, while contributing to security of supply in Greece and the wider Southeast European region. At the same time, it reinforces Greece’s position as a strategic regional energy hub.
